races.name: Rob Over The Hill EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Battle Fever
runners_data.comment: A £50,000 son of Sands Of Mali and half-brother to a modest performer at six furlongs, out of a dam without much to recommend her at five, he's from a yard short on form currently but with a strong record in this event, having been successful in it last year; a booked rider with a fine record at the track is a plus, though he otherwise looks up against it on debut, and a rating of 67 reflects a middling profile.

runners_data.name: Desert Move
runners_data.comment: Having been well beaten on a modest debut in a maiden at Hamilton, he drops significantly in trip to five furlongs today, which could bring about improvement, for a yard that has landed two of the last five runnings of this race; drawn wide, he carries a workable rating of 72 with room to progress.

runners_data.name: Enemy Action
runners_data.comment: He found things tougher when stepped up to six furlongs, finishing down the field in a seller at York last time, but dropping back to this shorter trip, regarded as his more effective range, could bring improvement, though there's still more for him to find; drawn wide, a rating of 74 keeps him in this mix as a value danger.

runners_data.name: Inca Warrior
runners_data.comment: By Invincible Army and a half-brother to a modest performer over seven furlongs, he's tough to fancy with any confidence on debut, especially with connections without a success from their last 22 runners; a rating of 67 reflects a workmanlike profile at best.

runners_data.name: Palm Reader
runners_data.comment: A costly breeze-up purchase by Blue Point out of a dam smart over six furlongs, he wears a tongue-tie for the first time and faces a stiff task on debut against more experienced rivals; a rating of 67 is respectable enough without making him easy to fancy.

runners_data.name: Waiting For Archie
runners_data.comment: A big, raw sort who ran to a similar level as his debut when beaten eight and a quarter lengths over seven furlongs in a maiden at Leicester last time, he's bred to appreciate more of a test than today's drop in trip and is drawn wide; his yard has landed two of the last five runnings of this race, but a rating of 64 leaves him with more to prove.

runners_data.name: Autumn Jewel
runners_data.comment: Effectively still finding her feet, she was well beaten on a truncated debut effort in a maiden at Musselburgh, and clear improvement is needed to be competitive here, though she is bred with plenty of speed and wears a hood for the first time; a rating of 65 leaves her towards the rear of these figures.

runners_data.name: Viking Barbie
runners_data.comment: Quickly into action again just a day after her latest start, she ran to form when second, beaten a length and a quarter, in a novice at Sandown, and remains capable of a bold effort over this sound-ground sprint trip; connections are short on form of late, but a rating of 77 keeps her as one of the leading dangers.

runners_data.name: Up The Stakes
runners_data.comment: Well beaten on a substandard debut in a novice at Newcastle, his only start so far, he has everything still to prove and sits at the bottom of these figures on a rating of just 42, leaving him hard to consider without more encouraging signs.

runners_data.name: Nightbloom
runners_data.comment: A serious pedigree on show, being a 400,000-euro daughter of Invincible Spirit, half-sister to a high-class sprinter, and out of a dam who excelled over six furlongs as a juvenile, she's fancied to open her account for a shrewd yard; a rating of 86 makes her the one to beat in this field.

races.name: Matthew Ireland Memorial EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: High Hazard
runners_data.comment: Having shown improvement from his debut when a keen-going second, beaten a length and a half, in a novice at this course last time, he has a leading chance if he builds on that; effective over this trip on good ground, and with a jockey boasting a fine record here, a rating of 81 puts him firmly in this mix.

runners_data.name: Rosberg
runners_data.comment: He showed promise on his sole start, finishing fourth, beaten six lengths, in a novice at Thirsk, and with more expected as he steps forward, this trip on good ground should continue to suit; a rating of 81 makes him one of the leading dangers here.

runners_data.name: Asander
runners_data.comment: A modestly-bought son of Saxon Warrior out of a dam who excelled at middle distances, he was born in mid-February and looks up against it on his belated debut against more forward types; the lowest of our ratings here reflects a stiff task first time out.

runners_data.name: Happy Love
runners_data.comment: Bred with plenty of quality, being a half-brother to a high-class performer at 8f and out of a dam who excelled over five furlongs as a juvenile, he catches the eye on debut, sent out by a yard with a strong record in this event, having been successful in it last year; a rating of 84 puts him firmly among the leading fancies.

runners_data.name: Under Arrest
runners_data.comment: Well held throughout after racing off the pace when beaten ten lengths in a novice at Newmarket on his debut, he should have that experience to call on now, with this trip likely to suit; a rating of 76 means there's more to prove against this field.

runners_data.name: Astral Calling
runners_data.comment: Bred to be smart, being a daughter of Space Traveller and half-sister to a performer who excelled at seven furlongs, she was a notable pedigree buy and is sent out by a yard firing on all cylinders (a 28% strike rate over the last fortnight); a rating of 86 makes her the most interesting runner in this field on debut.

races.name: George Kilburn Memorial Nursery

runners_data.name: Emerald Bay
runners_data.note: Ran three times without placing, best effort a sixth over 6f on Good; a natural hold-up horse whose trainer George Scott fires at 2/13 in the 14-day window, and P J McDonald is a significant booking — the redistribution to midfield reflects a crowded rear group rather than a change of tactics, so watch for a wide run late.
runners_data.comment: Comfortably held down at 5f in a novice at Windsor last time, this light-framed sort has yet to show a great deal in his starts so far; cheekpieces go on for the first time and, with the stable in good form, he could do better switching to handicaps for us at 54, though a month-plus absence since is a further concern.

runners_data.name: Farndale
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's yard is in strong form at 15/81 over 14 days, and Farndale steps back to 7½f after a placed effort at that trip on Good going — two of her three runs have come on similar ground with creditable form, and as a genuine hold-up type she needs the pace to set up properly for her finishing effort.
runners_data.comment: A slow start undid her chance at Chester latest, where she was ultimately well beaten in a seller, and results have been modest in her starts so far; bred to stay well and already proven over today's trip, she nonetheless remains difficult to fully trust for us at 65 as she steps into handicap company for the first time.

runners_data.name: Amantha
runners_data.note: Sole winner in the field, landing a 7f Good-ground contest last time having previously been campaigned at shorter; Brian Ellison's 2/23 14-day strike rate is modest but the horse's own form line over this trip and going is the standout data point in this race, and at 135lbs she carries a penalty that will need a strong run from the hold-up position.
runners_data.comment: Stepping up having recently landed a seller by a short head at Musselburgh, she's clearly come forward with that drop in grade and looks the type to take well to handicaps on debut in that sphere; suited by 7f on a sound surface, she rates the one to beat for us at 69 in a modest race, though the yard's recent cold spell is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Tiger In The Tree
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed front-runner, though flagged for fading in the finish across all three career starts — on a going report confirming Good to Firm, the uncontested lead is a significant tactical asset, but the fade pattern and lowest OR in the field (51) mean holding on in the straight is the key question rather than a given.
runners_data.comment: Beaten well back in a novice at Redcar most recently, she has struggled to make an impression in her starts to date; by a sprinting sire out of a mare suited by a mile, today's trip fits the pedigree, but on the evidence so far she's up against it for us at 45 as she tries handicaps for the first time.

runners_data.name: Happy Humpo
runners_data.note: Cheapest in the market on OR 46 with a fade flag in the data; Cieren Fallon takes the ride for Charlie Clover whose yard shows 3/13 over 14 days — this horse holds up naturally but is displaced into a midfield map position due to the cluster of closers, carrying a style-fit discount that weighs against a winning run here.
runners_data.comment: A well-beaten run in a maiden at Lingfield last time fell short of her seller-class form, continuing a modest start; sharper at 6f on good ground and fitted with cheekpieces for the first time, this light-framed sort looks the type to do better now she meets handicap company for us at 62, though it's been a month since that below-par effort.

races.paceDynamic: Tiger In The Tree is the sole confirmed front-runner in a five-runner field and will attempt to dictate from the front over 7½f at Beverley on Good to Firm ground, setting a sustainable rather than pressured tempo with no rivals likely to seriously contest the early lead. The three genuine hold-up horses — Emerald Bay, Farndale, and Happy Humpo — will track from the rear, while Amantha, also a hold-up type, brings the only recent winning form in the field. Happy Humpo and Emerald Bay are redistributed to midfield on the map because there are more true hold-up types than the rear of the pace picture can accommodate, meaning one or more will race closer to the pace than their natural style dictates. With Tiger In The Tree controlling an uncontested, measured gallop, this race shape strongly favours a progressive hold-up horse with a decisive turn of foot in the final two furlongs — a soft, controlled early pace punishes flat-out closers but rewards those who can quicken through the field once the tempo lifts.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Tiger In The Tree sets a comfortable, uncontested pace that sets up a strong finishing burst from the hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Tiger In The Tree dictates throughout on a soft lead, but the measured gallop leaves plenty in the tank for hold-up types turning for home, and the progressive closer with the best turn of foot wins late. This is the dominant shape given the lone front-runner and a field of genuine hold-up horses seeking ground in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Tiger In The Tree bowls along at a genuinely slow pace and the hold-up horses leave themselves too much to do.
scenarios.body: With only five runners and no pace rival, Tiger In The Tree could coast through the race in a near-canter, leaving chasers with too much ground to make up in time. Tiger In The Tree's fade tendency is a risk, but a truly dawdling gallop on good-to-firm ground could see the front-runner last home in a slowly-run sprint finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Improve
scenarios.trigger: If Emerald Bay or Happy Humpo, forced to race closer than natural, adapt well and turn their redistribution into a tactical advantage.
scenarios.body: Racing closer to the pace than usual could allow either redistributed type to avoid a traffic problem and quicken earlier than rivals who track further back, landing a blow before the true closers get organised. This shape is discounted because both Emerald Bay and Happy Humpo carry style-fit concerns, fading tendencies, and modest form figures.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Blanket Finish, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses mid-race and several horses hit the front simultaneously in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A messy race shape with no runner properly placed could compress the field into a tight finish where highest-rated or best-weighted horse prevails on raw ability. This remains the least likely scenario given Tiger In The Tree's confirmed front-running role, but the low OR band and juvenile inexperience across the field keeps it non-zero.

watchPoints.text: Tiger In The Tree has faded in all three career starts — watch whether the unchallenged lead translates to a genuine test of stamina in the final furlong or collapses late, as this will determine whether hold-up horses get to the winner.

Emerald Bay and Happy Humpo are both mapped to midfield despite being natural hold-up types — watch their positioning in the early stages to see if either actually races closer than expected, which would change the shape of the finish materially.

Amantha's penalty (135lbs) is the highest weight in the field and she is racing 12 days after her win — watch whether she travels with the same fluency she showed last time or looks in need of the run under the extra burden.

With only five runners on a Good to Firm surface at Beverley, the pace is unlikely to be truly strong — if the early splits are very slow, the entire hold-up strategy of the field is undermined and Tiger In The Tree's ability to control tempo becomes decisive.

races.name: Charlie Wood Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Al Aasy
runners_data.note: William Haggas's nine-year-old is the sole confirmed pace-setter here, and Cieren Fallon will have full control of the tempo; 77 days off and a prominent style that suits this uncontested lead role, though his OR of 114 and Good to Firm record (10/15 similar going) makes him a live force throughout.|
runners_data.comment: Talented but sometimes hard to fathom, he returned from a short break to finish runner-up in a Group 3 at Newbury; this quick-ground test over a trip he handles well suits, and a rating of 120 makes him the one to beat.

runners_data.name: By The Book
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's five-year-old arrives on a 98-day break with solid course-and-distance form (3rd at 14f, Good), and while he is naturally a front-running type, the presence of Al Aasy means Dougie Costello will likely be unable to secure his preferred position and must race closer to midfield than ideal.|
runners_data.comment: Back from a short break, he was below form at the top level when well held in a Group 1 at Meydan; now stepping down in grade over a trip he stays and ground he handles, a rating of 115 makes him a leading threat.

runners_data.name: Involvement
runners_data.note: Simon & Ed Crisford's five-year-old is 27 days fresh and has recent good-ground form, but being a genuine forward-goer by nature, Oisin Orr faces the task of accommodating a horse that wants to be prominent into a space already occupied by Al Aasy and contested by several others of the same style.|
runners_data.comment: He was well beaten in a Listed race at Goodwood last time, unable to last out 12 furlongs on the softer ground, though quicker conditions today may help him see out the same trip more effectively, aided by a jockey with a fine record at this course; stamina remains the obvious question given his figures suggest he's sharper around 10 furlongs, but a rating of 107 keeps him firmly in this mix.

runners_data.name: Miss Wong
runners_data.note: David Simcock's four-year-old is the only authentic hold-up runner in the field, wearing a hood and stepping back up to 1m4f where her two best runs (1st, 2nd) have come; Connor Beasley will be hoping a compressed early tempo brings this rare closer into contention, but the Good to Firm record (4/10 similar going) is modest and the weight concession is significant.|
runners_data.comment: She raced up to her mark without truly seeing out 14 furlongs when well beaten in a Group 3 at York last time, and steps back into handicap company sporting first-time cheekpieces; this shorter 12-furlong trip should suit, and a rating of 100 puts her firmly among the contenders.

runners_data.name: Percy's Daydream
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's four-year-old comes in just 11 days after his last run, boasting strong recent form (1st, 4th, 0, 1st) on Good ground, but his naturally prominent style — the best-fitting of the redistributed runners on raw recent form — means Mark Winn will have to compromise position behind Al Aasy rather than race where this horse thrives.|
runners_data.comment: Progressive and race-fit having won a handicap at this course by four lengths last time, she nonetheless faces a stiff step up in grade here and, on a rating of 100, appears to have a good deal of improvement to find against this level of opposition, even with the trip and ground both in her favour.

runners_data.name: Phantom Flight
runners_data.note: Listed as NON-RUNNER — George Scott's seven-year-old does not take part and should be disregarded entirely from any race-shape assessment.|

races.paceDynamic: Al Aasy is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival to press him, Cieren Fallon can dictate terms at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m4f trip on Good to Firm ground at Beverley. The field is unusually congested with prominent-style runners — By The Book, Involvement, and Percy's Daydream are all natural forwardly-placed types, but with Al Aasy already filling the lead role, these three are likely to be shuffled back into a midfield pack they would not naturally occupy. That compression in the early stages will create a steady-tempo race with a long, drawn-out finish rather than a lung-bursting sprint, as the backmarkers have limited genuine hold-up horsepower to generate a late surge. This shape strongly favours the horse who can travel prominently just behind Al Aasy and quicken off a soft pace — a true front-running or close-tracking profile that handles Good to Firm ground will be at a premium, while horses pushed out of their natural role in the reshuffle face an uphill task to impose themselves.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Soft Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Al Aasy dictates an uncontested, moderate gallop and the prominent pack settles tamely behind him, favouring whoever can track and quicken.
scenarios.body: Al Aasy controls every yard from flag to finish on a comfortable lead, and the horse best placed to track him — ideally one with class and a quick turn of foot on Good to Firm — pounces in the straight; the slow tempo means no advantage to deep hold-up runners.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Shuffles Late
scenarios.trigger: If the compressed midfield of By The Book, Involvement, and Percy's Daydream produces a three-way move turning in that swamps a tiring Al Aasy.
scenarios.body: The redistribution of prominent types into mid-pack creates a mass challenge in the straight as multiple horses hit the front simultaneously; whoever finds a clear run earliest from that group wins the tactical scrum.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly falsely slow and collapses late, giving a genuinely held-up runner a rare winning opportunity at Beverley.
scenarios.body: Miss Wong, the only true hold-up runner, would need the pace to be slow enough to compress the finish into a short sprint on Good to Firm ground; her best form (2nd, 1st) has come on similar ground but she is giving weight away and her course record is poor.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Develops Chaotically
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent-heavy field produces early jostling for position that forces a faster-than-expected early pace and tightens the finish to one furlong.
scenarios.body: A contested early tempo would expose Al Aasy to pressure he rarely faces and could bring the closers into the race earlier than expected; however, without true hold-up horses to capitalise, the race would likely still fall to a prominent type who had settled best early.

watchPoints.text: Al Aasy stealing an uncontested lead: if Cieren Fallon is allowed to bowl along in front unchallenged at a dawdle, the rest of the field may find it impossible to reel him in on Good to Firm ground before the straight ends.

Percy's Daydream and By The Book crowding the early mid-pack: with three prominent types all seeking the same position behind Al Aasy, watch for bumping or awkward passage in the first half-mile that could compromise any of their runs.

Miss Wong's wide draw and hold-up style: Connor Beasley will need a truly compressed, sprint finish to make her hold-up profile relevant — if the gallop is even moderate, she faces too much ground to make up on Good to Firm.

Phantom Flight confirmed non-runner: the field has effectively dropped to five, removing one of the higher-weighted runners (133lbs) and tightening the shape analysis to a more straightforward solo-leader dynamic.

Trainer freshness flags — By The Book (98 days) and Al Aasy (77 days) both return after significant breaks; Haggas and Appleby both have strong records returning horses fresh, but condition off a long break is worth monitoring on fast ground.

races.name: Weatherbys Global Stallions App Coconut Cup Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Lexington Express
runners_data.note: Progressive three-year-old for Marco Botti ridden by PJ McDonald, has won three of her last four and handles this trip well on similar going; a natural prominent racer ideally placed to track the pace and deliver a straightforward challenge.
runners_data.comment: A confirmed front-runner who sets a strong pace, she failed to last home when fourth, beaten 11 lengths, from an identical mark last time, but dropping back in trip today should suit a filly who likes to dictate up front on a sound surface, and first-time cheekpieces may sharpen her further.

runners_data.name: Enamorus
runners_data.note: Stepping up in trip from recent seven-furlong form under Oisin Orr for Hugo Palmer; form has been inconsistent lately and the unfamiliar mile-and-a-half on Good to Firm demands more stamina than she has yet proven she possesses.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, she was below form down the field in a handicap at Sandown last time, but her official mark has eased, cheekpieces go on for the first time, and a jockey with a fine record at this course takes the ride; a rating of 84 suggests she's better than that effort and can play a leading role.

runners_data.name: Come On Eibhlin
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Dylan Cunha, fresh from a run nine days ago which is unusually quick back; handles this going and trip fine but will need a stronger-than-expected gallop to get competitive from off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in her recent starts, she raced keenly but ran to form when beaten two lengths off a pound higher mark at Newmarket last time, and with the trip and surface both to suit, she can go well again; a rating of 79 keeps her right in this competitive heat.

runners_data.name: Cancelled
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon takes the ride on this five-year-old for Jonjo & AJ O'Neill, wearing a tongue-piece; 48 days between runs is a concern and the hold-up style will be harder to deploy when the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to pull her through the field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her recent starts, she was below form when well beaten in a handicap at Hamilton last time, but first-time cheekpieces plus a trip and surface she handles well could spark improvement; drawn wide in a field of ten, she needs to bounce back.

runners_data.name: Alessia Fernanda
runners_data.note: Six-year-old veteran for Declan Carroll who won last time out over this trip on Standard ground, wearing a tongue-strap; Good to Firm is fine but trainer has had no winners from seven runners in the last 14 days, and the hold-up style requires more generous fractions than this pace map projects.
runners_data.comment: Her form has been up and down, and she raced too keenly from off the pace when well beaten last time off a mark one pound higher than today's; drawn wide and effective around this 7-9 furlong range, first-time tongue-tie may help settle her, but on a rating of 74 she remains hard to trust on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Porth Eilian
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's three-year-old is the sole confirmed front-runner and Connor Beasley will look to roll forward unchallenged; the STYLE_FIT tag reflects she is stepping into the lead role somewhat against type, but her recent course-and-distance form (won over 8f at Beverley on Good) suggests she can make it count if allowed a comfortable lead.
runners_data.comment: She confirmed her form when third, beaten four lengths, from an identical mark last time, and with the trip and surface both suiting again on this sound going, she looks capable of running well once more; a rating of 85 puts her firmly among the leading contenders.

runners_data.name: Sandy Craic
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's three-year-old won on Good ground at seven furlongs and this step up in trip looks well-timed; sits comfortably in the prominent group and Mark Winn can tuck her just behind Porth Eilian, making her a logical threat in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Returning to form emphatically to land a handicap by half a length off a two-pound lower mark at Carlisle last time, this filly now looks to be building confidence on the back of that success, and with conditions on this good-to-firm ground suiting, a rating of 89 puts her clear at the top of these figures.

runners_data.name: Vitality
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's three-year-old is a genuine front-runner by nature — Jason Hart will want to race prominently — but with Porth Eilian, Lexington Express, and Sandy Craic all ahead of her in the queue, she is likely to find herself further back than ideal, which tempers her prospects materially.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in four starts, she was below form when well held in a handicap at Nottingham on her handicap debut last time, and needs to find more on that evidence, though this trip and good ground have suited her in the past; a rating of 73 leaves her toward the foot of these figures.

runners_data.name: Ma Leila
runners_data.note: Tom Clover's lightly-raced filly has a short form string and is unexposed at this distance; by inclination she wants to race up with the pace, but the traffic ahead of her means Ryan Sexton may be forced to settle her in a more withdrawn position than suits, compromising her chance.
runners_data.comment: Winless but with more improvement expected now she's tackling handicaps, she matched her debut level when third, beaten six and a quarter lengths, in a maiden at Thirsk last time, and with this trip and ground suiting, a rating of 80 makes her a strong contender to note.

runners_data.name: Sogniamo
runners_data.note: Won over nine furlongs at Goodwood on Good ground last time for David O'Meara and Ben Robinson, giving her live form claims stepping back to this trip; a natural prominent racer whose recent win suggests she handles quick conditions, and she gets first run on the redistributed horses.
runners_data.comment: She weakened quickly and failed to stay 10 furlongs when well beaten in a handicap at Redcar last time, and though today's step back to 8 furlongs is shorter than her best trip of 9f, it should still suit better than the longer test that undid her; drawn wide, a rating of 71 leaves her the outsider of this group on these figures.

races.paceDynamic: Porth Eilian is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m½f at Beverley on Good to Firm ground. Lexington Express and Sandy Craic will press from prominent positions, but neither is a natural pace-forcing type, meaning the tempo is unlikely to become truly searching. This setup — a single, uncontested pace-setter over a flat mile-and-a-half on fast ground — classically suits prominent racers who can track close to the pace and pounce in the straight, rather than deep closers who need a truly honest gallop to generate momentum. The field holds more front-running or prominent types than can all realistically slot into their favoured position: Vitality and Ma Leila are natural prominent racers who will find space ahead of them occupied, with Porth Eilian, Lexington Express, and Sandy Craic best-placed to secure the prime early berths.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Porth Eilian Front-Runs Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Porth Eilian bowls along uncontested and the pace is conservative enough to preserve her stamina reserves to the line.
scenarios.body: Porth Eilian sets a measured fractions, controls the tempo throughout, and has enough left to kick again when challenged in the Beverley straight on Good to Firm ground that she handles; front-runners who can dictate here are notoriously hard to peg back when the pace is honest but not punishing.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Porth Eilian's lead is swallowed up in the home straight by a horse that has tracked her from just off the pace.
scenarios.body: A horse like Lexington Express or Sandy Craic, sitting a length or two off the front throughout, benefits from the controlled fractions and produces a sustained challenge once balanced into the straight; this scenario rewards horses with course-proven stamina at this trip on quick ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closer Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is deceptively strong and the front runners empty, allowing a midfield horse to finish through beaten rivals.
scenarios.body: Come On Eibhlin or Cancelled, tracking from midfield, get a smooth run up the straight and arrive in time as the prominently-placed horses tie up; this scenario requires a stronger gallop than Porth Eilian's likely metronomic pace suggests, making it the least natural outcome of the field shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse — Closers Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent horses push forward early, creating an unexpectedly contested pace that sees the front rank fold in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Redistributed runners Vitality or Ma Leila, unable to find their natural position, may inadvertently push the pace by crowding the early stages and leave the door ajar for genuine hold-up types; however, this scenario is markedly discounted because neither Vitality nor Ma Leila are true hold-up horses, and the hold-up contingent in this field lacks the depth to capitalise reliably.

watchPoints.text: Porth Eilian's lead is entirely unchallenged — if Connor Beasley is allowed to dictate a soft early fractions, the winning margin could be deceptive and front-runners who get away cheaply at Beverley are notoriously hard to reel in.

Vitality and Ma Leila are both natural front-runners who will find themselves blocked from their preferred positions; watch for early crowding or jostling as their jockeys attempt to push forward against the natural order of this pace map.

Lexington Express is in career-best form with three wins in her last four, and PJ McDonald is likely to track Porth Eilian closely — if she gets a clean slot in second position, she becomes the primary danger to the front-runner in the straight.

Cancelled has been off for 48 days and is the heaviest-weighted runner in the field at 142lbs; if she reappears short of peak fitness the hold-up strategy becomes even harder to execute in a moderate pace scenario.

Sogniamo's jumping-up win over 9f at Goodwood on Good ground gives her a recent strong form line, but her stable companion Sandy Craic means David O'Meara will have two horses pressing from prominent positions — watch how they are deployed relative to each other early.

races.name: Weatherbys Racing Bank Handicap

runners_data.name: Capital Guarantee
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's hold-up performer has shown enough on good ground at this sort of trip (second over 8f in similar conditions) to be respected, but recent form is patchy and from the rear it will need a genuinely honest pace to get involved.
runners_data.comment: A below-form run at York last time, 21 days ago, continues a moderate spell, though he was runner-up earlier in this sequence of starts; suited by 7-8f on any going, this winless sort is hard to trust on the balance of the evidence despite a rating of 80 for us in his favour.

runners_data.name: Highland Olly
runners_data.note: Grant Tuer's five-year-old has excellent recent form, winning twice over 8f on good ground, and Alistair Rawlinson will look to press forward from an early stage; four wins and five places from 15 similar-going runs underlines a strong claims as a prominent racer who thrives when up with the pace.
runners_data.comment: A pair of wins sit among his last six starts, and he was beaten only a half-length in second last time from a mark just 1lb lower; front-running when conditions allow and effective at 7-9f on soft or good to firm, he has solid claims for us at 80 with the yard in good form, though he can also find one too many.

runners_data.name: Degale
runners_data.note: David & Nicola Barron's runner has one win and four places from 11 runs on comparable ground, but its natural instinct to race at the back of the field means it has been placed in midfield on the map — it will likely race further back than shown and will need more pace than this race shape is expected to generate.
runners_data.comment: Little went right at Carlisle last time, well beaten down the field to continue an up-and-down profile of finishes; drawn wide today at 8f on a sound surface he handles, this winless sort is hard to trust for us at 71, the widest slot in the field a further complication.

runners_data.name: It Just Takes Time
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front runner in this field; Mark Walford's eight-year-old has crept into the frame twice over 7f on good ground recently and Jack Garritty should get a clean lead, though an absence of pressing rivals means the tempo may not be strong enough to prevent the hold-up horses catching him late.
runners_data.comment: Twice runner-up in his last two starts, he was beaten only a head off a mark 2lb lower last time at Thirsk; effective at 5-7f on any ground, this still-winless sort rates a strong threat again at 90 for us despite an 18-day break.

runners_data.name: Glenfinnan
runners_data.note: Michael Dods' six-year-old won over 8f on good ground not long ago and Connor Beasley has been booked; a natural hold-up horse with headgear worn, it will need the pace to be honest and the distance to test the leaders to get competitive from off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Fitted with a first-time hood, he won three starts back and was only beaten 2l in fourth last time under an unchanged mark; effective at 6-8f on soft or good to firm, he remains fairly treated by the weights and rates a threat again for us at 82, with two so-so efforts in between the only blot.

runners_data.name: Tattie Bogle
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's four-year-old is in excellent form (2-1-2 in last five on good ground), has returned quickly after just three days, and Jason Hart will look to be prominent; with wins over 7f and 8f on good going, this is a horse in great nick whose style ideally suits racing close to a single pacemaker.
runners_data.comment: Rock-solid of late with four places and a win from his last six starts, he was beaten only a half-length in second last time off an identical mark to today's; suited by 6-7f on a sound surface, he's the one to beat on our figures at 90, with a quick reappearance after just 3 days the only thing to note.

runners_data.name: Coolree
runners_data.note: Sam England's seven-year-old is a genuine front runner or close-up prominent racer by nature, evidenced by three wins and five places from 15 similar-going runs, but with Tattie Bogle and Highland Olly also wanting to be forward, Oisin Orr may be unable to secure the position this horse needs; tongue tie worn and operating off a low OR of 69 gives an obvious pull in the weights.
runners_data.comment: Fitted with a tongue-tie and cheekpieces for the first time, he has two wins among his last six starts and was only beaten 2l in second last time from a mark just 1lb lower; equally happy at 8-10f in any conditions, he can build on that form again and rates a strong threat for us at 85, with the extra gear the only new variable to watch.

runners_data.name: Bajan Bandit
runners_data.note: Patrick Morris' six-year-old wears a visor and has no wins or places from 15 runs on comparable good ground — form on standard/all-weather surfaces is far more typical of this horse; a true hold-up type whose map position in midfield flatters its likely race position, and the step up in trip and going quality are both concerns.
runners_data.comment: A well-beaten effort at Nottingham last time extends a run of modest finishes, with turf form still very much unproven; better served by 7-8f and clearly happier on the all-weather, he wears a visor for the first time today but, rated 77 by us, still has plenty to find before he can be trusted.

races.paceDynamic: It Just Takes Time is the confirmed front runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Jack Garritty should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over this 7½f Beverley straight course on Good to Firm ground. Tattie Bogle and Highland Olly will look to press close to the pace in prominent positions, creating a competitive but not punishing early tempo that should reward those who travel smoothly through the race. Coolree is a natural prominent type but, with Tattie Bogle and Highland Olly also wanting to be forward, Coolree is likely to be shuffled into midfield against his wishes, reducing his effectiveness. This controlled, single-paced shape over a flat track on fast ground favours hold-up horses with a strong finishing kick — provided the pace is genuinely honest — but the predominance of prominent runners at the head of affairs means the race is likely to be won by a horse travelling comfortably just off the pace rather than from the deep rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If It Just Takes Time sets a steady, uncontested tempo and the race only quickens in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A single, uncontested front runner on fast ground at Beverley over 7½f rarely produces a truly searching gallop, meaning the race compresses into a sprint finish; horses who travel economically just off the pace through the middle of the race will arrive with the most energy.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is brisk enough that It Just Takes Time, Tattie Bogle and Highland Olly pull clear early and the hold-up horses are left with too much to do.
scenarios.body: A competitive three-way battle for the front two or three positions could generate enough pace to string the field out, rewarding those who took prominent positions and controlled their energy from the front third of the race.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely fast and the front runners tie each other up, leaving room for a strong finisher to pick them off.
scenarios.body: Glenfinnan or Capital Guarantee, both natural hold-up performers with course-relevant form at this trip on good ground, would benefit if the race is truly run — though the controlled single-paced shape makes this outcome less likely given the true hold-up types have been pushed toward midfield.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, All-the-Way
scenarios.trigger: If It Just Takes Time meets no pressure whatsoever and is allowed to coast in front at a crawl, turning it into a pure sprint.
scenarios.body: A virtually uncontested lead at a walk would suit It Just Takes Time to steal the race on the bridle, though its recent form shows limited finishing speed and it carries the highest weight in the field; this scenario requires complete passivity from all other jockeys.

watchPoints.text: Tattie Bogle has run just three days ago and Jason Hart will need to manage that freshness carefully — if he over-commits chasing It Just Takes Time early, a quick reappearance could find him out late.

Coolree's inability to secure its natural prominent position in a field this competitive is a material concern — Oisin Orr will need to make an immediate decision at the start about whether to force the issue or settle for a less comfortable role.

Highland Olly's recent winning form over 8-9f on good ground is strong, but dropping back to 7½f on a flat, straight track tests whether that form translates — watch whether Rawlinson opts to press hard or conserve.

Bajan Bandit's going record on turf good/good-to-firm (1 run from 15 in similar conditions, no wins or places) is a significant red flag; if the ground remains Good to Firm, expect this runner to be well beaten.

With the going described as Good to Firm throughout the card and multiple races already run on the same surface today, monitor any late going updates — faster ground will further compress the finish and increase the advantage of those racing prominently.

races.name: Happy Birthday Roy Archer Handicap

runners_data.name: Battenburg Belle
runners_data.note: Front-runner who has won or placed in four of her last five starts including a win at 6f on Good; stepping up to 7½f is the key question but a slow pace of her own making helps; Rebecca Menzies sends her in on just 12 days' rest suggesting fitness is not a concern; STYLE_FIT tag is present only because she is listed as Prominent — in reality she is the confirmed pace-setter here.
runners_data.comment: Full of running when landing a handicap by a head last time from a mark 2lb lower than today's, she's rounded off that sort of form with three seconds and a win among her last six starts; suited by 6f on soft or good to firm, she's the pick for us at 69 in a modest race, though the yard's recent quiet spell is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Zoulette
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning after 32 days with Ollie Sangster hitting form (1 from 27 over 14 days); best effort was a second at 7f on Good which makes the trip and going combination acceptable, but six previous course-distance results without a win question her ability to make the most of a decent pace shape.
runners_data.comment: A well-held effort at Wolverhampton last time fell short of her best, though she was runner-up two starts earlier; suited by 5-7f on good to firm or the all-weather, this yet-to-win filly could have more to offer for us at 57 if bouncing back from a stale run after a month-plus absence.

runners_data.name: Forever Twenty
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator — Jason Hart rides a horse whose natural position is at the rear, nudged toward midfield on the map only because this field has a surplus of backmarkers; form of 3rd at 7f Good is encouraging but recent 10th and 6th on the same trip and going are flat, and Ivan Furtado's yard is without a winner from 20 runners over 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Beaten 6l when below form at Doncaster last time, she'll need to bounce back from that effort; sporting cheekpieces for the first time and suited by 7f on quick ground or the all-weather, this winless filly is up against it for us at a rating of 57 following a moderate recent sequence.

runners_data.name: Walk On Walk On
runners_data.note: Races from the rear by nature and is represented here in midfield purely as a consequence of several horses sharing the same role; fourth at 7f on Good is the standout piece of recent form, but the Noel Wilson stable (0/4 over 14 days) offers little confidence, and the horse has failed to win from 11 runs on comparable going.
runners_data.comment: A modest fifth beaten 6l up at 1m at Ayr last time did at least point to progress after a quiet spell; better suited back at 6-7f on any going, cheekpieces go on for the first time and, with his mark drifting lower, this winless sort for us at 56 still needs more before he can be trusted.

runners_data.name: Hood Wink
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's yard is the most active and in-form handler in this field (15/81 over 14 days); Hood Wink wears a hood, has three consecutive top-four finishes at 8f on Good, and is the most reliable closer in the race, though the hold-up style means she needs a strong gallop that this pace shape may not generate.
runners_data.comment: Consistency has been the theme lately with two thirds and a fourth, and he matched that level again in third last time, beaten 2l from a mark 1lb higher than today's; sharp at 1m on most going including the all-weather, first-time blinkers could sharpen him up further for us at 64, though he still needs to find extra to land his next win.

runners_data.name: Maid On The Shelf
runners_data.note: Prominent runner from the Charlie Johnston yard (9/65 over 14 days) who steps back to 7½f after finishing seventh at 9f and fourth at 10f; the drop in trip and faster ground both appear positive, and she should slot in just behind Battenburg Belle where she gets a clear run without expending energy fighting for position.
runners_data.comment: A well-beaten effort in a maiden at Hamilton latest continues a modest opening to her career, rarely threatening the front rank; bred to appreciate further ground around 10f, she may do better now she tackles handicaps for us at a rating of 46, though she still has plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Truly Special
runners_data.note: Holds up from the rear and won over 6f on Soft before three modest efforts on Good; Connor Beasley in the saddle adds a measure of confidence but the Wainwright yard is cold (0/3 over 14 days) and the 26-day absence combined with the fast ground and a field of hold-up types competing for the same late-race ground makes this a speculative interest at best.
runners_data.comment: Landing a handicap by three-quarters of a length last time from a mark 2lb lower than today's, she did so with a willing attitude that marks her the type to progress; best at 7-8f on soft or good to firm, though less effective on the all-weather, she can follow up for us at 65 if building further on that form.

races.paceDynamic: Battenburg Belle is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only Maid On The Shelf likely to push into a prominent position alongside her, she faces minimal early pressure and should control a sustainable gallop from the front over Beverley's 7½f on Good to Firm ground. That tempo — honest but uncontested — shapes this as a race where the lead is not surrendered cheaply, and the sectionals are unlikely to be severe enough to cause Battenburg Belle to tie up in the straight. The three redistibuted hold-up types (Forever Twenty, Walk On Walk On, Hood Wink) have been pushed forward on the map only because the field contains more natural hold-up horses than the shape can accommodate; in practice all three will race toward the rear, meaning closers must produce a significant finishing kick to reel in a front-runner who is never pressured. The dominant tactical verdict is that a front-running or prominently-raced profile is the one most favoured here — a controlled pace on fast ground with no genuine pace duel gives the leader every chance to last home.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Belle Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Battenburg Belle dictates an uncontested lead and Maid On The Shelf settles just off her through a measured pace.
scenarios.body: Battenburg Belle sets a comfortable rhythm on Good to Firm ground, conserving enough energy to repel any late challengers; her recent sequence of placed and winning efforts at 6f suggests she can sustain pace into 7½f under these conditions. Maid On The Shelf, tracking the leader, is best placed to pounce if Belle weakens but the Charlie Johnston handler is yet to hit form over this trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closer Delivers From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough to set up a late finish and one of the genuine hold-up runners produces a sustained run.
scenarios.body: Hood Wink has consistent 8f form on Good ground with placed efforts and headgear (b) sharpening focus, making her the most credible of the backmarkers if a closing run is rewarded; however, this scenario requires a faster early tempo than this race shape suggests, making it the second-most-likely but still considerably less probable. Truly Special, who has won over 6f on Soft and placed over 8f on Good, represents the each-way interest if the finish opens up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses late and a horse tracking midfield delivers a well-timed challenge through the pack.
scenarios.body: Zoulette, operating off a 32-day break, ran second at 7f on Good ground and sits at a workable mark; if she travels well mid-division she could pick off tired rivals late. Walk On Walk On has shown form at this trip and going combination but the Noel Wilson yard is without a recent winner and the horse is out of its natural role here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Battenburg Belle overcooks the fractions on fast ground and fades inside the final furlong, opening the race to a scramble.
scenarios.body: Forever Twenty showed a third at 7f on Good and is the most unexposed of the hold-up runners if the race falls apart; however, the yard (Ivan Furtado, 0/20 over 14 days) is not in form and the horse's recent 10th on the same trip and going is a concern. This scenario relies on conditions and tactics conspiring against the favourite and is assigned low probability accordingly.

watchPoints.text: Battenburg Belle's ability to stay 7½f is the pivotal question — if she flags inside the final furlong having led throughout, Maid On The Shelf is ideally positioned to capitalise.

Hood Wink is the most in-form closer in the field but needs a genuinely strong gallop to close from the rear; watch to see whether the pace Battenburg Belle sets is brisk enough to justify a hold-up ride.

The surplus of genuine hold-up types (Forever Twenty, Walk On Walk On, Hood Wink, Truly Special) means the rear of the field will be congested; watch for traffic problems in the straight if the leader is tiring and all four make their challenges simultaneously.
Going is Good to Firm across all races at Beverley today — any rain or significant change should be monitored as it would alter sectionals and benefit the hold-up runners more than the front-runner.

Tim Easterby's yard strike rate (15/81 over 14 days) stands well above every other trainer represented here — Hood Wink's chance should not be underestimated purely because the pace shape is unfavourable.
